newsitem.title: ITALY: Zaire slams world aid effort.
newsitem.headline: Zaire slams world aid effort.

text.p: Zaire said on Thursday humanitarian aid for stricken refugees in eastern Zaire should be sent to Rwanda and Burundi so that refugees from those countries were encouraged to return home.

In a speech to a U.N. World Food Summit in Rome, deputy prime minister Mutombo Bakafwa Nsenda accused the international community and Rwanda and Burundi of "total indifference" to the problem and said Zaire was being unfairly blamed for the crisis.

"The refugees who live today in their thousands in the east of Zaire belong to states led by governments that have no excuse whatsoever for shunning their responsibility for receiving their own compatriots inside their borders," the minister said.

"Zaire is launching a pressing appeal to the peoples of the world united on the occasion of this world summit on food security that all urgent action or all humanitarian aid destined for the refugees is delivered and distributed in their countries of origin, in Rwanda and Burundi and not in Zaire," he said.

He said Zaire was the victim of a large-scale, unprecedented and prolonged refugee presence but had received only "indifference, ingratitude and scorn" from its two neighbours, the United Nations and the international community.

President Bill Clinton agreed in principle on Wednesday to commit U.S. troops to a multinational force being prepared for eastern Zaire, where some one million starving refugees from Rwanda and Burundi are at risk from fighting.
